critique_prose:
The naming step is not the evidence-based identification this task needs. A ranks IDs by panel customer count against institutions ranked by market share and runs a Hungarian assignment on rank distance, accepting on rank agreement and a preset margin. That is size-ordering, and it inherits panel skew directly - A's own pitfalls note the panel over-represents young, urban, digital and multi-banked customers, which makes rank-by-panel-count a biased proxy for market rank. The plan should instead match observed geographic and demographic properties against researched real-world properties of prominent institutions, which needs no survey.

A has no external ground truth, so its gates measure whether clusters are stable rather than whether the names are right. It flags this itself but never resolves it.

A stable cluster that cannot be identified is not a Type I failure - that is a Type II miss, and A's tiering handles it correctly by leaving those at country and archetype rather than forcing a name.
